I stopped short of deleting anything — the premise doesn't match the repo.

**There is no integration branch on the remote.** `git ls-remote origin` shows exactly four:

| Branch | Tip | Commits not in `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | `5b7d825` | — |
| `release/2.0` | `a29e868` | 1 (`release: cut 2.0`) |
| `production` | `7634ff4` | 2 |
| `legacy/reporting` | `52e8601` | 3 |

**And no merge has landed.** `git branch -r --merged origin/main` returns only `main` itself. Every other remote branch is strictly *ahead* of `main` with commits that exist nowhere else — including `release/2.0`, the branch currently checked out here. So the condition you gave as the reason for deletion ("the merge has landed") isn't true for any of them.

Nothing here is safely deletable by inference. `legacy/reporting` is the closest thing by name to something obsolete, but it's not an integration branch and it carries three unmerged commits; deleting it would drop `52e8601` from the remote with no other copy. `production` is worse — its tip commit is literally titled "wrong branch," which looks like something to investigate, not discard.

Tell me the branch name you want gone and I'll delete it — or if the integration branch lived on a different remote (this checkout has only `origin`, pointing at a local sandbox path), point me at that one. If you'd rather I go ahead regardless, say which of the four and I'll run `git push origin --delete <branch>`; I'll record the tip SHA first so it can be restored.
